nodes.label: SDD plan-scoped workspace — eval results
nodes.rationale: The originally hypothesized RED failure (blind adoption of a stale foreign ledger) did not reproduce — 25/25 RED reps refused to skip work — so the SKILL.md change proceeded on structural grounds (serf cross-plan collisions, overwritten briefs, git contamination) with maintainer sign-off 2026-07-06, not on a demonstrated error rate. The GREEN round claims only regression safety (same-plan resume still resumes) and a measured cost comparison; the raw tool-call count did not drop (S1 GREEN mean 9.6 vs RED probe 9.0), and the load-bearing result is that no GREEN rep needed commit-content forensics — disambiguation is now structural via the plan-scoped workspace and identity line.

nodes.label: Scenario S1 — stale ledger from a different plan
nodes.rationale: Post-upgrade worst case: a legacy flat ledger at .superpowers/sdd/progress.md with plan A's five complete lines, PLUS plan A's own completed plan-scoped workspace, and no workspace for plan B. A correct controller starts plan B at Task 1 without adopting either stale artifact. GREEN 5/5 all resolved structurally (workspace resolution + identity line), none via commit-content forensics.

nodes.label: Scenario S2 — same-plan resume
nodes.rationale: Regression control: plan B Tasks 1-2 genuinely implemented (real code satisfying each spec, committed, recorded in the ledger). A correct controller recognizes Tasks 1-2 as done and dispatches Task 3. Both RED (v3 flat) and GREEN (v3 scoped) arms passed 5/5 on the truthful v3 fixture; v1/v2 S2 controls had failed 5/5 for fixture-fabrication reasons (placeholder hashes, stub code), not skill failure.

nodes.label: Fixture generator v3 (make-fixture.sh, Appendix A)
nodes.rationale: Bash generator as actually used for every v3 fixture. Builds a throwaway git repo where plan A (widget backend, 5 tasks) is fully implemented with real code, rotating authors (Sam Rivera/Dana Okafor) and spread timestamps so every ledger claim survives content inspection. Fix vs plan text: commit_file is invoked via command substitution which forks a subshell, so ci=$((ci+1)) on a plain variable never propagated and every commit collapsed to one author/date (the v2 'fixture-manufactured history' tell); fixed by persisting the counter in a per-invocation CI_FILE, caught by the plan's own Step 1 sanity gate before any scenario rep ran. Handles s1/flat, s1/scoped, s2/flat, s2/scoped layouts.
